channel.title: Resources on Vibe Coding
channel.description: Recent content in Resources on Vibe Coding

item.title: Model Context Protocol Docs
item.description:
The official home for the Model Context Protocol specification: how the handshake works, how tools and resources are defined, and reference documentation for building both clients and servers.

Start here if you want to understand MCP at the protocol level rather than just using pre-built servers from the directory.

item.title: Claude Code GitHub Repository
item.description:
The public GitHub repository backing Claude Code — where releases are tracked, issues are filed, and changes to the CLI agent are documented over time.

Useful for checking what changed in a recent release, filing a bug, or seeing how other users are running into and working around specific issues.

item.title: Anthropic Engineering Blog
item.description:
Anthropic’s engineering blog covers practical, implementation-level writing on building with AI — agent design patterns, evaluation methodology, and lessons from building Anthropic’s own tools.

A good source for grounded, non-hype thinking on why certain agent architectures work better than others.

item.title: Simon Willison's Blog
item.description:
Simon Willison writes frequently and specifically about AI coding tools — hands-on reviews, careful benchmarking, and clear-eyed commentary that cuts through a lot of the surrounding hype.

Particularly useful for grounded takes on how well a new tool or model actually performs at real coding tasks, rather than marketing claims.

item.title: Latent Space
item.description: Latent Space covers the AI engineering space through both a newsletter and podcast, with interviews and deep dives that regularly touch on coding agents, developer tooling, and the people building them.

item.title: r/ClaudeAI
item.description: A community forum where people share real workflows, prompt patterns, and troubleshooting specific to Claude and Claude Code — useful for seeing how other practitioners are actually using the tools day to day, warts and all.

item.title: Hacker News
item.description: Hacker News isn’t AI-specific, but new coding tools and agent releases show up there early, and the comment threads often include genuinely critical, hands-on feedback rather than pure marketing response.

item.title: GitHub Topic: AI Agents
item.description: GitHub’s topic pages aggregate repositories tagged with a given subject — in this case, AI agent frameworks and projects — sorted by popularity and updated automatically as the ecosystem moves.

item.title: Learn Prompting
item.description:
A free, structured course covering prompting techniques from fundamentals through more advanced patterns, independent of any single vendor’s tools.

Not coding-specific, but the underlying skills — clear task framing, few-shot examples, structured output — transfer directly into working with coding agents.
